dedupe_keys.name: usgs national seismic hazard model 2023 50 state update

description: The National Seismic Hazard Model is the USGS probabilistic model of earthquake ground shaking hazard for the United States. The 2023 update covers all 50 states, and its data release (Petersen and others, published 21 December 2023, DOI 10.5066/P9GNPCOD) includes the seismicity catalogues, hazard curves and uniform-hazard ground motions. It is produced by the USGS Earthquake Hazards Program with partners. The data release is available free from USGS ScienceBase, and USGS media and data are in the public domain. Caveats: values are probabilistic exceedance levels for given return periods, so scenario or event-specific studies need separate ground-motion modelling. The model is the basis for seismic provisions in US building codes, and USGS notes its use in design of pipelines, bridges and dams, which makes it a standard hazard input for infrastructure seismic risk and fragility analyses; a related record is the GEM Global Seismic Hazard Map.
